question.problem:
Determine if the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}8 & 9 \\ -4 & -4\end{aligned}]$
is diagonalizable or not, and if it is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 9 \\ -4 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (8-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )-9\cdot (-4) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda -32+36 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +4 & =0 \\ (\lambda -2)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=2.$ Since we get one repeated eigenvalue, the matrix might not be diagonalizable. To check this, we row-reduce the matrix $(A-2I)\text{x}=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 9 \\ -4 & -4\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ -4 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{2}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has only $1$ pivot column. This implies that we will have only $2-1=1$ linearly independent eigenvector corresponding to the current eigenvalue. Therefore, $A$ is not diagonalizable.
